_why: D-158: the CITE runs are the strongest external evidence this project has, and until
this file existed they were re-earned by somebody remembering. This is what a nightly
FAILURES ONLY, and that is deliberate. The 2026-08-26 note is explicit that scope is
not comparable between runs -- 420 assertions attempted one day and 395 another, on
unchanged code, because TEAM Engine attempts what the capabilities document lets it.
So a total that moves is not a regression and cite-count.py does not treat it as one.
A failure is: it means an assertion was attempted and the answer was wrong.
Lower a baseline in the same commit that earns it. Raising one is a decision about
what this server claims, and belongs in an ADR rather than in a passing build.

note: The recorded hand run of 2026-08-21 was 405 of 420 with a different scope. What is
comparable between them is the failure count, and both are what they are because
the untested share is large: WFS 2.0's suite skips whole conformance classes when
the capabilities document does not advertise them, and this server advertises the
ADR-042 condition 3 records the run that discharged it: 0 failed, 25 skipped. The
24 untested here are the same shape -- Part 2 assertions this server does not claim.
Six is the number ADR-041 condition 6 recorded when it was discharged by running
it -- 187 passed, 6 failed -- and it is a baseline rather than a target. It is the
only non-zero one here, so it is the only place a regression could hide behind an
existing failure; the count is exact for that reason.
